Part 1: lesões persistentes

Maxwell Says: "From ácido to Thunder, you'll find all manner of injury, insult, infection, and affliction listed below. It is my humble hope that you witness only enough of them to keep you comfortably in business."

 

How to Use This Section

Below you will find three different sections. The first section is the lesão persistente tables themselves. Your characters will roll on these tables to determine what manner of injury or affliction they've received. Second are the Anatomy Tables. You may need to use these tables to determine location of a cicatriz or injury. The third section contains the mechanical effects for two new conditions, não funcional and ausente. Some lesões persistentes may apply one of these effects to a membro or other body part.

All these tables are not included in this Journal Entries but are in a table compendium, they will be pulled automatically by automations (if enabled). You can always use the chat command /mmmm to bring up the table selector. The chat command can also be used to directly roll a specific table (eg. /mmmm Radiant)

 

When Do Characters Role na lesão persistente Tables?

There are two different circumstances that will cause characters to Role na Linger Injury tables:

Critical Hits. Any time one of your characters receives a Critical Hit from any source (combat, traps, spell attacks, etc.) they roll 3d6 on the table that matches that dano Type. If the Critical Hit deals more than one type of dano, they Role na on the table for the type that dealt the majority.

Critically Failed Saving Throws. Any time one of your characters critically fails a Saving Throw that would cause them to take dano (including spells, traps, environmental effects, etc.) they roll 3d6 on the table that matches that dano Type. If the failed Saving Throw would cause them to take more than one type of dano, they Role na table for the type that dealt the majority.

 

Step By Step

1.Role na lesão persistente Tables

The character receives a Critical Hit or critically fails a Saving Throw. Allow them to roll 3d6 to determine the injury or affliction they'll receive.

2. Role na Anatomy Tables, if needed

Some options may have you roll on an Anatomy Table to determine the location of the injury or cicatriz. The DM may always directly choose the location instead of rolling if it better fits the situation's narrative. If, by chance, you roll a situation that is physically impossible or simply doesn't make sense given the established narrative (one of your characters takes shrapnel to their left leg when it is already ausente, for example), then there is no effect, and the character (luckily) escapes the situation without an injury.

3. Narrate the Injury and its Effects

The DM narrates the result of the injury and describes any of its mechanical effects to the player. You may need to consult information in the section that describes the não funcional and ausente conditions.

4. Tratamento

Some (though not all) injuries are treatable. Tratamento allows characters to reduce the duration of injuries, or even potentially cure them altogether. Unless otherwise stated, any Tratamento that requires a Wisdom (Medicine) check takes one action. In general, it is assumed that each character will have one opportunity to attempt this Wisdom (Medicine) check. The DM may allow repeated attempts at a failed Tratamento check at their discretion, but after a success further Tratamento attempts are not allowed (to further decrease the injury’s duration).

Assume that all characters are aware of the information in the Tratamento section of the lesão persistente charts and understand how to tend to these injuries. As long as a character has a Healer's Kit it is assumed they will have any equipment needed for a Tratamento that requires a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

Some more serious injuries will require surgery to treat. Surgery is a skill challenge described in Part 2 of this book. Even if an injury has no Tratamento listed, the DM is welcome to work with the character to find a cure that works well dentro de the campaign's narrative.
